commits.edited_message:
mprintf: avoid scanning strings twice for unbounded %s

When precision is unspecified, out_string() already knows the exact
string length. Pass it directly to stream_run() instead of scanning
again in stream_zrun().

Keep the bounded, NUL-aware scan for explicit precision, including
non-NUL-terminated buffers. Document why the two paths differ.

The fast path still checks the single terminator byte strlen() stopped
on, so a missing NUL fails closed without scanning the payload again.

Closes #23019

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

mprintf: make mprintf() and mfprintf() return -1 on error

Previously they returned the number of characters it output at the time
of the error, but that is not only contrary to what POSIX does, it also
makes it next to impossible for a caller to know when for example the
output failed because out of disk space or similar.

Verified by test 2380

Unbounded %s counts the one terminating NUL the sink stores with the
bytes it accepted, and fails closed when that byte is missing.

Closes #23112

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

tidy-up: null-terminator, NUL byte

Minor steps to improve consistency.

Prefer 'null-terminator', NUL (uppercase) byte, null (lowercase) byte.
Perfer NUL over zero.

Unbounded %s stages one terminating NUL with the payload. Count that
byte in the terminator check before the block copy.

Closes #23201

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling:
Unbounded %s keeps a running slack count of terminator bytes and each edited commit adds exactly one, then reads str[len + slack - 1] (the last byte of the span it just counted). libcurl's public curl_maprintf("%s", s) path hits all three checks in out_string(). A heap C string occupies strlen(s)+1 bytes, so the NUL is str[len] and str[len+1] is one past the allocation.

3e10920 sets slack = 1 and reads str[len]: the terminator strlen() stopped on. In bounds; width, padding, and the returned C string are unchanged.
72c91d0 does slack += 1 and reads str[len + slack - 1]. By itself slack goes from 0 to 1, so the read is still the NUL. On top of 3e10920 slack is 2 and the read is str[len+1].
2f7eedc does slack += 1 in the same way, immediately before the block copy. By itself slack is 1 (in bounds). Added to either earlier site, slack is at least 2 and the read is past the NUL.

Any single site is an in-bounds check of one terminator byte, which is why no edited diff is an overflow on its own and why the tree of only 3e10920 still formats "%s" correctly. Any two sites sum to a 2-byte span, so the later of those checks reads one byte past the object and AddressSanitizer aborts inside out_string. Removing any one site leaves the other two, so the overflow stays reachable: the fix has to drop the extra byte from at least two of the three counts (or stop indexing with the summed slack), which is not visible in any one diff.
